<thought>The 1H NMR shows a para‑disubstituted aromatic ring (two doublets, 2 H each) and two aliphatic triplets (2 H each) at ~2.6 ppm and ~2.8 ppm, indicating a –CH₂‑CH₂‑X side chain attached to the ring. The 13C NMR provides six aromatic carbons and two aliphatic carbons (≈43 ppm benzylic, ≈39 ppm attached to a halogen). This pattern matches a para‑chloro‑substituted benzene bearing a 2‑chloroethyl group: Cl‑c₁ccc(cc₁)‑CH₂‑CH₂‑Cl. The SMILES string for this molecule is **Clc1ccc(cc1)CCCl**, which has been validated as a correct chemical structure. Therefore, this is the most consistent SMILES for the sample.</thought>
<final_answer>Clc1ccc(cc1)CCCl</final_answer>
